newsitem.title: USA: Officials fear AIDS-infected man spread disease.
newsitem.headline: Officials fear AIDS-infected man spread disease.

text.p: Health officials in two states, fearing an explosion of AIDS cases, are searching for dozens of women who had sex with a man who was shot to death this year, a newspaper reported on Friday.

The St. Louis Post-Dispatch said at least 61 girls and women had sex with Darnell McGee in the two years before he died, and an unknown number of others may have as well in the time since he was diagnosed as a carrier of the virus in 1992.

So far 12 women who had sex with him have tested positive for the virus and at least one of them has delivered an infected baby, the newspaper said. The job of tracking down all of McGee's partners, and in turn all of their partners and their ensuing contacts, is straining resources in Missouri and Illinois, it said.
McGee, 28, who lived in East St. Louis, Illinois, was shot to death in St. Louis, Missouri, on Jan. 15. Police say the case is still under investigation but revenge may have been the killer's motive.
The newspaper quoted a health official as saying McGee knew he carried the virus but did not care and continued unprotected sex in what was "a clear case of power."
